name: Basic Jump
description: Both feet leave the ground together, the rope passes once underneath, and you land softly on the balls of your feet. Every other move in RopeBeat is a variation on this single rhythm.
tips: Keep hops low — a few centimeters off the floor is enough room for the rope.
Turn the rope from your wrists, not your shoulders, so your arms stay relaxed and close to your body.

name: Run-In-Place
description: Instead of landing on both feet, you shift your weight foot to foot like a light jog, lifting the free knee between each rope pass.
tips: Picture jogging on the spot — the rope is just along for the ride.
Keep the lifted knee low; height comes from speed, not from kicking higher.

videos.title: How To Do A RUN IN PLACE JUMP ROPE | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide

name: Side Swing
description: No jump at all — you swing the rope beside your hip, back and forth, without it passing underneath you. It's the move you'll drop into between tricks to reset your rhythm.
tips: Keep your elbow tucked and let your forearm and wrist do the swinging motion.
Practice this before a trick that starts from a swing, so the transition into the jump is seamless.

videos.title: Ultimate Guide To Jump Rope Side Swings

name: Skier
description: Both feet stay together and jump side to side over an imaginary line, the way a skier's feet move down a slope, while the rope keeps turning underneath at the regular one-per-jump pace.
tips: Keep the side-to-side hop small — a shoulder-width sway is plenty.
Let your knees absorb the landing so the swing doesn't bounce up into your shoulders.

name: Front and Side Straddle
description: Feet open out to the sides on one jump (side straddle) and open front-to-back on the next (front straddle), alternating like a slow jumping-jack while the rope keeps the same single-pass rhythm.
tips: Open your feet only as wide as feels controlled — balance matters more than width here.
Practice the front/back version separately from the side version before alternating them.
